title: Archive 100 research ideas: results, failures and untested proposals
body:
Publishes the available October 10 research campaign, including unsuccessful experiments and execution gaps, plus the October 11 continuation after PR364.

**The 100-item plan is not 100 completed tests.** Every idea has an indexed outcome and evidence links in `research/campaign-100-results/README.md`, with JSON and CSV copies. Forty ideas have no located execution result; analytical memos, partial experiments and blocked work are labeled separately.

Included: 16 original final reports; 1,075 selected raw evidence files in lossless archives with per-file SHA-256 provenance; ten architecture-prototype outputs, including two no-positive-root failures; decoder failure logs; and PR366's completed local replay receipt. The separate 100-architecture proposal list is retained without claiming it was fully executed.

The summary explicitly preserves corrections: invalid dangling-node improvements, noisy historical labels, exact-kappa/J ranking disagreements, hypothetical layouts later refuted, incomplete centre-lemma proofs, and builds stopped before final verification. Historical reports are preserved as data and have not all been re-executed. Their baseline/cap differences and finite search scopes are stated.

Validation: `python3 -B research/campaign-100-results/validate_archive.py` passes locally, checking all 100 IDs, CSV/JSON agreement, counts, evidence links, provenance, 1,075 archived members and the complete file manifest. The dedicated GitHub archive-integrity workflow also passed on Python 3.11 and 3.14 at head `fa8ab946df57ebadae1a470b637c2a590a0a5317` ([run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38112606459)). Published README, results JSON and manifest were independently fetched from GitHub and matched byte-for-byte. This verifies the archive, not every historical mathematical claim.

The unchanged three-file source-pin repair from PR318 is included for repository CI, as in PR366. No mathematics is changed by that repair. The archive adds no unconditional theorem or global-optimality claim.
